learn.title: Four quiet steps
learn.body: When you run `clang hello.c -o hello`, four steps happen without a word: preprocessing, compiling, assembling and linking. This unit opens the box, one stage at a time. The first stage is the preprocessor, a text editor that runs on your source before the compiler sees it.

learn.title: Lines that start with #
learn.body: A line that starts with `#` is a directive for the preprocessor, not C code. `#include` pastes the text of another file at that spot. `#define NAME text` makes every later `NAME` turn into `text`.

learn.title: A constant with #define
learn.body: Before compiling, `LIMIT` is replaced by `10`, so this prints 20.

learn.title: Look at the result
learn.body: The `-E` flag stops after preprocessing and prints the text. Your own lines come last, after all the pasted header text.

learn.title: A macro only swaps text
learn.body: Take `#define SQ(x) x*x` and the call `SQ(1+2)`.
steps: The preprocessor does no maths, it only swaps text

learn.body: Wrap each macro parameter, and the whole body, in parentheses. Then the swapped text keeps its meaning.

questions.prompt: Which of the four steps runs first?
questions.explanation: The preprocessor handles `#include` and `#define` lines before the compiler reads anything.

questions.prompt: What does `#include` do with a header such as `stdio.h`?
choices: Pastes the text of that header file in its place
questions.explanation: `#include` is a text paste done by the preprocessor.

questions.prompt: Which flag makes `cc` stop after preprocessing and print the result? Type it.

questions.explanation: The preprocessor swaps text and does not calculate. The compiler later turns `5 + 1` into 6.

questions.prompt: With `#define SQ(x) x*x`, what does `printf("%d", SQ(1+2))` print?

choices: The parentheses keep each argument together

questions.prompt: Match each item to what it does.
questions.explanation: Each one is plain text work done before the compiler starts.
